Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office deputies responded to the scene around 11:15 p.m. near the intersection of Northwest 24th Avenue and 63rd Street in the Gladeview neighborhood. Responding deputies located a man suffering from an apparent gunshot wound to his upper extremities. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue medics arrived and transported him to a nearby hospital in stable condition. Authorities have not released details about a possible suspect or the circumstances surrounding the violence. Anyone with information is urged to reach out to Miami-Dade Crime Stoppers at 305-471-8477.

headlines: HILTON MIAMI BEACH MERGES FIVE HISTORIC BUILDINGS FOR 2027 OPENING
HISTORIC ART DECO BLOCK IN MIAMI BEACH REOPENING IN 2027
SEE HOW FIVE HISTORIC MIAMI BEACH BUILDINGS ARE UNITING
draft.article: Hilton Miami Beach is scheduled to open in early 2027 at 2000 Park Avenue in the Museum Historic District. The 289-room hotel will restore and unite five historic properties across nearly an entire city block following years of vacancy and a 2012 fire. Dating from 1938 to 1953, the restored structures highlight Streamline Moderne and Miami Modern designs. Notable buildings include Henry Hohauser's 1939 Collins Park Hotel, L. Murray Dixon's 1938 Adams Hotel, and Albert Anis's 1940 Tyler Hotel. Situated near Lincoln Road and Ocean Drive, the property will offer three swimming pools, multiple dining concepts, and tropical gathering venues.

items.desc: Three Haitian American women secured seats on school boards across South Florida this election cycle, while Marly Métayer came close to winning the Coral Springs commission seat held by her slain daughter.

headlines: THREE HAITIAN AMERICANS ELECTED TO SOUTH FLORIDA SCHOOL BOARDS
HISTORIC SCHOOL BOARD VICTORIES ACROSS SOUTH FLORIDA
SOUTH FLORIDA SEES FIRST HAITIAN AMERICANS ON SCHOOL BOARDS
draft.article: South Florida made history this election cycle as three Haitian American women secured public school board seats in Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties. Cynthia Alcéus Dominique, Christina Romélus, and Linda Cothière are the first elected officials of Haitian descent to serve on these regional school boards. The milestone establishes unprecedented representation across the region's public education system. Dieudonne Joisil, a public school educator in Fort Lauderdale for nearly 40 years, recognized the breakthrough of having Haitian American leaders on all three major local boards. Meanwhile, in Coral Springs, candidate Marly Métayer fell short on November 3 of securing the city commission seat previously held by her slain daughter, former Vice Mayor Nancy Métayer.
